name: Giganotosaurus
description: Giganotosaurus was one of the largest theropods to ever walk the Earth, living during the Late Cretaceous period around 98 million years ago in what is now Argentina. Reaching up to 43 feet in length and weighing nearly 8 tons, this massive predator was larger than Tyrannosaurus rex, though it had a more slender build built for speed. Its serrated teeth and powerful jaws made it an efficient hunter, likely preying on large herbivores like Argentinosaurus. Unlike T. rex, Giganotosaurus had a longer skull and three-fingered hands, suggesting a different hunting strategy. As one of the top predators of its time, this fearsome carnivore ruled the South American landscape before the rise of even larger titans.

name: Kentrosaurus
description: Kentrosaurus was a genus of stegosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic period, approximately 155 to 150 million years ago. It was a relatively small member of the stegosaur family, measuring around 4.5 meters (15 feet) in length and weighing up to 1.5 metric tons. Kentrosaurus is known for its distinctive double row of bony plates and spikes that ran along its back and tail. The plates were smaller and more pointed compared to its more famous relative, Stegosaurus. Towards the tail, these plates transitioned into long, sharp spikes, which likely served as a formidable defense against predators. Kentrosaurus had a small head with a beak-like mouth, suited for a herbivorous diet consisting of low-lying plants. Its fossils have been primarily found in what is now Tanzania, Africa. The discovery of Kentrosaurus has provided valuable insights into the diversity and evolution of stegosaurs, as well as their ecological role during the Late Jurassic period.

description:
**Nom** : *Didymograptus sp.*.

**Description** : Les graptolites appartiennent à l’embranchement des Hémichordés, à la classe des Graptolithacés. Ils vivent en colonies (rhabdosome) constituées à partir d’un individu initial appelé sicule. Un stolon chitinisé constitue l’axe central de la colonie et possède un nombre variable de branches, les stipes. Le stolon comporte une série de thèques, petite loge latérale, où vivent les individus composant la colonie. Chez *Didymograptus*, les thèques disposées sur un axe double.

name: Agama boueti  - MNCN41779
description:
**Description**: This 3D model features the Mali Agama, a lizard species specialized for life in dry environments such as deserts and savannas. It is a scientifically priceless specimen, serving as the holotype for the species. The species is well-known for its sexual dimorphism, where males display dark body colors with contrasting white markings, in contrast to the more cryptic, brownish tones of the females. This visualization provides a high-resolution look at the definitive individual used by Chabanaud to define the species over a century ago.

**Specimen**: *Agama boueti* (Chabanaud, 1917).

**Inventory number**: MNCN-41779

**Collection**: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales, Herpetology. Curator: Marta Calvo (mcalvo@mncn.csic.es).

**More about**:

Find more about the MNCN [here](http:mncn.csic.es/en).

Find more about the collection [here](http:mncn.csic.es/es/colecciones/cientificas/herpetologia).

name: ~ The Gentle Sea ~
description:
Hi! It's been awhile since I uploaded anything, so here we go again! So instead of my usual "3D-ify a 2D drawing" approach, I decided to try to make a scene that represents how I feel in a way that's unique by just using inspo references of a bunch of animals, coral, foilage, etc. I've been feeling extremely low lately, so I figured I'd label this "The Gentle Sea" because I feel like I should be more gentle and less harsh on myself. It encompasses some of my favorite things in the world, such as pastel colors, water, bubbles, and other cutesy stuff! I wanted to make something that brought me joy simply to look at. So I set out to accomplish just that. I struggled really hard to complete this one, but we eventually got there and I'm really proud of it!!

As always, if you notice anything wonky or wrong, don't hesitate to let me know.
I'm still working on a Twitch channel / YouTube to showcase how I create these as well, so don't worry, that's coming! <3
